entities.name: Catholic Apostolic Church
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Catholic Apostolic Church (Irvingites), founded in London in the early 1830s around the charismatic ministry of Edward Irving (1792-1834) — a Scottish Presbyterian minister whose congregations at Regent Square experienced the restoration of speaking in tongues (glossolalia) and prophecy beginning in 1830 — was the first modern Christian community to experience and institutionalize charismatic gifts, making it the direct forerunner of the Pentecostal and Charismatic movements that today encompass 600+ million Christians worldwide.

Edward Irving's Regent Square congregation began experiencing what participants believed to be miraculous gifts of the Holy Spirit in 1830 — including speaking in tongues, prophecy, and healing — a full 70 years before the Azusa Street Revival (1906) that launched Pentecostalism. Irving, though died in 1834 before the Church was fully organized, inspired the movement; the Catholic Apostolic Church was formally organized with twelve 'apostles' (to restore the primitive church) beginning in 1835.

The Catholic Apostolic Church developed an elaborate liturgy combining Catholic, Anglican, and Eastern Orthodox elements — believing it was restoring the complete primitive church before Christ's imminent return. When the twelve apostles died without being replaced (the last in 1901) and Christ had not returned, the church entered terminal decline, though German and Dutch branches (becoming the New Apostolic Church in 1863) survived with replaced apostles. The New Apostolic Church, with approximately 10 million members, is the Catholic Apostolic Church's living descendant — making the Irvingites indirectly ancestral to one of the world's fastest-growing churches.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Catholic Apostolic Church — hosting the first modern outbreak of glossolalia (1830), institutionalizing charismatic gifts 76 years before Azusa Street, and being ancestral to the New Apostolic Church (10 million members) and indirectly to the entire Pentecostal-Charismatic tradition (600+ million Christians) — is one of Christianity's most consequential 19th-century religious movements.
